READING

**Establishing the timeline**

Application validated 2026-08-14. Adding the three planning scenarios gives determination dates of approximately:
- Target (13 weeks): 2026-11-13
- Median (34 weeks): 2027-04-09
- Slowest (61 weeks): 2027-10-15

Adding 22 weeks of construction to each:
- Best case ready: ~2027-04-13
- Median case ready: ~2027-09-08
- Worst case ready: ~2028-03-15

The critical dates against which those completions must be measured are:
- 44/44A bid due: 2027-09-14
- Hallowbrand lease ends: 2027-11-30
- New 44/44A contract starts: 2028-03-31 (implied by the contract end date and the bid cycle)
- Culverstone deposit holds the option until: 2028-06-30

**Dead-mileage arithmetic**

Culverstone is 3 miles further from Verrancombe Bridge. Each of the 22 vehicles working the 44/44A network does at minimum one return dead run daily (out to first stand, back after last duty). That is 6 extra miles per vehicle per operating day.

22 × 6 × 313 × £0.63 = £26,029 per year

The rent differential stated in the brief (£96,000/year) is rent only. The genuine annual net advantage of Culverstone is approximately £70,000/year after dead mileage.

**Ten-year cost comparison**

ARDENSHAW:
- Rent at £214,000 × 10 = £2,140,000
- No capex, no interim complication
- Total exposure: £2,140,000

KESTERWICK (median planning, no Nethercote gap needed):
- Capex: £40,000 deposit + £480,000 works = £520,000
- Rent at £118,000 × 10 = £1,180,000
- Dead mileage premium × 10 = £260,000
- Total: £1,960,000
- Net saving vs ARDENSHAW: ~£180,000

KESTERWICK (worst-case planning, 3.5-month Nethercote gap Nov 2027–Mar 2028):
- Add ~£65,000 Nethercote; add unquantified workshop-outsourcing cost
- Net saving narrows to roughly £100,000–£115,000 before those unquantified costs

**Liquidity check under KESTERWICK**

Current position: £640,000 cash + £200,000 undrawn facility = £840,000 headroom. Deploying £520,000 on the deposit and works leaves £120,000 cash plus the £200,000 facility — adequate, but the buffer is thin for a 31-vehicle operation if any other working-capital pressure arises, particularly during a prolonged Nethercote period.

**The 44/44A bid is the pivot point**

The problem states unambiguously: *"depot cost goes into the bid as a fixed line."* The bid is due 2027-09-14. The next contract starts 2028-03-31.

Under ARDENSHAW: Trentmoor writes in £214,000 with absolute certainty, regardless of anything the planning authority does.

Under KESTERWICK — median scenario: consent arrives ~2027-04-09, construction completes ~2027-09-08. That is six days before the bid submission deadline. The bid would have been prepared in July–August when Culverstone is still a building site; they would be pricing on an expected cost they have not yet physically occupied. Six days is not a margin — it is the absence of one.

Under KESTERWICK — anything beyond the median: if determination runs above roughly 47 weeks from validation, consent will not have been granted by bid day. There is then no credible Culverstone cost to insert as a fixed line. The realistic depot cost at bid time would be Nethercote at £18,500/month (£222,000/year annualised) — actually slightly worse for competitive purposes than ARDENSHAW's £214,000. Alternatively, Trentmoor bids on an anticipated Culverstone cost it has no planning permission to use, which is a misrepresentation risk in a public tender.

How likely is planning at 47+ weeks? The authority's own median is 34 weeks against a 13-week target — a 2.6× ratio. Planning timelines in this class are rarely symmetric; the distribution almost certainly has a right tail. The three recorded data points (13 target, 34 median, 61 worst) are consistent with a distribution where perhaps 25–35% of applications run above 47 weeks. That is one application in three to four landing in territory that damages the bid.

**What the competitive bidding angle does and does not do for KESTERWICK**

It is correct that under median planning Trentmoor could bid the 44/44A renewal at a depot cost of roughly £144,000 against a competitor holding a Hallowbrand-equivalent lease at £214,000 — a £70,000/year structural advantage that could be decisive in a tendered margin. That is the strongest argument for KESTERWICK and it is genuine.

But the argument only works cleanly if planning is at or below the median. In the 25–35% of cases where it is not, the competitive advantage disappears and the bid risk emerges. The reward (competitive advantage in a single tender) is uncertain and one-shot; the risk (mispriced fixed line in a multi-year contract for 71% of the fleet) is structural. The asymmetry does not favour accepting it.

**Planning refusal is a separate tail risk not priced in the brief**

If consent is refused — not delayed, refused — the £40,000 deposit is gone, the Hallowbrand offer has expired (deadline 2026-12-19, deposit deadline 2026-12-05), and Trentmoor is hunting for a permanent depot from a standing start before November 2027. This scenario is not quantified here but its existence is another argument for not staking the Hallowbrand certainty on a planning outcome.

**Workshop continuity**

Nethercote has no workshop. Trentmoor runs 31 vehicles. Any period at Nethercote requires outsourcing all preventive and corrective maintenance. The cost is unquantified but non-trivial, and the operational dependency on third-party workshop availability introduces scheduling risk for the contracted service.

**Summation**

The financial case for KESTERWICK is real: a ~£180,000 net advantage over ten years in the median scenario. But that figure is approximately 8.4% of the total ten-year outlay under ARDENSHAW, and it is predicated on a planning authority that is demonstrably and chronically behind its own targets. The single event that matters most commercially in the next 18 months — the 44/44A bid — requires a fixed depot cost. Certainty in that fixed line is worth a premium. ARDENSHAW delivers it unconditionally. KESTERWICK delivers it only if a laggard planning authority moves at or below its median pace, and even then with days to spare rather than months.

---

READING
  The planning authority runs its median determination at 2.6 × its stated 13-week target. The 44/44A contract bid, due 2027-09-14, requires depot cost as a fixed line; under the median planning scenario Culverstone construction completes just six days before that deadline and under any slower outcome consent has not been granted at all. The net annual saving from Culverstone (~£70,000 after dead mileage, against a 10-year all-in advantage of roughly £180,000 in the base case) does not justify the probability — conservatively 25-35% — that Trentmoor either cannot price its core contract correctly or prices it against a cost base it has no permission to use. ARDENSHAW removes that risk entirely for a premium of roughly £70,000 per year.

CALL
  ARDENSHAW

GROUNDS
  The planning authority's median determination is 2.6 times its stated 13-week target, creating a meaningful probability that consent will not be in hand when the 44/44A bid must be submitted with depot cost as an unqualified fixed line, and the circa-£70,000 net annual saving from Culverstone does not adequately compensate for that risk to the contract on which 22 of Trentmoor's 31 vehicles depend.
